title: Regional config parity incident: quant-mode mismatch causing canary degradation
body:
Summary:

On 2024-11-01 we observed a subtle but reproducible quality regression in EU canary traffic after a staged rollout of model:v2024-11-01. Latency and throughput were nominal but top-k token-level distributions and downstream embedding similarity drifted relative to baseline, causing elevated user-visible fuzziness in a small subset of requests. Canary error rates did NOT spike and health checks passed.

Why this is unique/dangerous: the issue only showed up as semantic drift (differences in model outputs) rather than hard failures. This escaped typical latency/CPU/GPU SLO alerts and required metric-level quality checks to catch.

Detection:
- 2024-11-01 08:14 UTC: automated canary-eval job (daily-qa-suite) flagged an embedding recall drop (eu-canary job) from 0.912 -> 0.817 relative to baseline for our internal eval set.
- 08:17 UTC: SRE oncall (Evan) got paged by quality-alert (alert id 9921).
- 08:25 UTC: Initial manual triage confirmed outputs in eu-prod-canary diverged from us-prod-canary for identical prompts.

Impact:
- Canary region only (EU). ~2% of production-like sessions routed to canary saw degraded similarity/semantic quality; no increased latency or retries.
- No customer-facing incidents reported. This was caught by synthetic evals.

Immediate timeline and actions:
- 08:30 UTC: Rolled back canary route to previous model variant in eu (model:v2024-10-16) using routing-control service.
- 08:33 UTC: Re-ran canary QA suite, eval scores returned to baseline. Canary traffic stable.
- 09:00 UTC: Created JIRA SRE-8271 and started postmortem working doc (this doc).

Investigation notes (what we looked at):
- Config parity between regions: compared all runtime flags and model-serving config between eu and us canaries.
- Weight artifacts: checksummed shards and verified checksums matched upstream artifacts.
- Runtime kernels: checked kernel selection logs; same kernels chosen.
- Quantization metadata: inspected quant profile metadata embedded in model package.
- Tokenization/normalization: quick cross-check to ensure tokenizer artifacts identical.
- Serving runtime version: confirmed identical git SHA of serving runtime.

Root cause (conclusion):
- A configuration propagation bug in the config management service (config-propagator v0.43) omitted a new flag introduced in the model onboarding flow: model.quant.profile_override. The flag was present in US clusters but not in EU clusters due to a condition in the propagation rules (region-specific filter introduced inadvertently in PR #1337).
- As a result, EU canary used the model package's default quantization profile (legacy int8-profile-v1) while US canary used the updated profile (int8-profile-v2) that the model was calibrated against. The mismatch produced consistent but subtle differences in token probability distributions and embeddings.

Evidence supporting root cause:
- Config dump from us-canary includes model.quant.profile_override=int8-profile-v2; eu-canary dump lacked any override key.
- Reproducing locally by running model with int8-profile-v1 vs int8-profile-v2 reproduces the eval delta seen in canary.
- PR 1337 changed propagation rules; revert diff shows region filter added the week prior.

Why checksum and serving logs looked normal:
- Weight files were identical and checksums matched; the model artifact behaved differently purely because a different quant profile parameter was applied at runtime, not because of corrupted weights or kernel selection.

Mitigation taken:
- Short-term: rolled canary traffic to the previous model variant in EU (complete).
- Immediate config fix: manually updated EU config with model.quant.profile_override=int8-profile-v2 and re-ran the canary evals in a controlled window (confirmed match to US). Change applied at 2024-11-01 14:12 UTC.
- Hotfix PR: revert the region filter in config-propagator and add a unit test that ensures new flags are included across regions (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/config-propagator/pull/210).

Longer-term fixes/action items (owners and due dates):
- SRE/Platform (Evan) - 2024-11-10: Add a config parity check to CI that compares a canonical flag set across regions when onboarding a new model version. (Test: run config-diff on every model roll.)
- Applied ML (Priya) - 2024-11-15: Add robustness checks in canary QA for "profile-sensitivity" – synthetic tests that run the model with alternate quant profiles and check for large deltas.
- Development (Luca/Jordan) - 2024-11-07: Merge PR to config-propagator to remove region-specific filter and add e2e test (PR #210).
- Observability (Samira) - 2024-11-12: Create an alert rule for cross-region embedding drift detection: if eu.canary.embedding_recall / us.canary.embedding_recall < 0.95 for 3 consecutive runs, page SRE.

Runbook updates (immediate edits to runbook suggested):
- Add a new checklist item under "Canary quality failure": always run 'config-diff --region eu --region us --model <name>' to verify flag parity before rolling out.
- Under "Model onboarding checklist": require explicit model.quant.profile_override field in the onboarding manifest; fail onboarding if absent.
- Add a section "Semantic drift detection" describing daily-qa-suite thresholds and how to interpret embedding/LMQA deltas.

Queries/commands used during triage (notes to self):
- config-diff --regions eu,us --model model:v2024-11-01  # showed missing key in eu
- curl -s https://config-propagator/api/v1/flags?region=eu | jq '.model.quant'
- kubectl logs -n prod-eu deploy/model-serving | grep "quant.profile" -A5 -B2
- python ./tools/eval_compare.py --host eu-canary:8080 --host us-canary:8080 --prompts qa_set.json

Open questions / unresolved items:
- Why did automated canary rollout tests not detect the missing flag? (Possible gap: config-diff was optional in the deployment pipeline.)
- Should we treat quantization profile as part of the model artifact (i.e., bake into the artifact and disallow runtime overrides) to avoid divergence? Tradeoffs: flexibility vs strict reproducibility.

Communication notes:
- Notified product and model owners at 2024-11-01 10:05 UTC (Priya led the notification).
- Drafted a short internal note for the weekly SRE sync and for Model Ops: "EU canary semantic drift due to config parity issue".

Post-incident metrics to be tracked:
- Number of model rollouts in last 90 days that had region-propagation differences.
- Frequency of config-propagator region filters changing in PR history.
- Improvement in time-to-detect semantic drift after adding cross-region embedding alert (target: detect within 30 minutes of rollout).

Lessons learned (brief):
- Config parity across regions is as important as artifact parity for deterministic behavior.
- Semantic/quality regressions require specific QA where usual SRE telemetry (latency/cpu/memory) is insufficient.
- Small config-propagator changes can have outsized blast radius when the change is a filter/selector.

Next steps (short):
- Merge hotfix PR #210 to config-propagator and roll it to staging for smoke tests (Luca).
- Implement the CI config-parity gate and add to model onboarding pipeline (Evan + Platform).
- Add cross-region embedding drift alert (Samira).

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep a copy of the exact config-dumps from both clusters in the artifacts folder for SRE-8271.
- Re-check other regions (ap-south, ap-northeast) for similar holes; we only looked at eu/us during fire.

Appendix: short reproduction steps for an engineer who picks this up:
1) Pull model package locally and start two local serving instances with different profile overrides.
   export MODEL_PACKAGE=/tmp/model-v2024-11-01
   ./serve --model $MODEL_PACKAGE --quant.profile=int8-profile-v1 --port 9001 &
   ./serve --model $MODEL_PACKAGE --quant.profile=int8-profile-v2 --port 9002 &
2) Run the eval script: python ./tools/eval_compare.py --host localhost:9001 --host localhost:9002 --prompts qa_set.json
3) Confirm embedding recall and top-k token distribution differences match the numbers in the initial alert payload.

If you pick this up, please append any additional evidence, especially any logs showing config-propagator errors around 2024-10-28 (when PR 1337 landed).

-- Samira
